Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Pankaj Bhatia,J.
1. Heard learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A. and perused the record.
No one appears on behalf of the complainant despite service of notice.

2. The FIR in question was lodged on 14.05.2024 initially as a missing person report alleging that the daughter of the informant aged about 17 years was enticed by the applicant on the false pretext of marriage and was missing.

Subsequently, in the statement of the victim recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C., the victim stated that she knew the applicant for the last two years, she also stated that physical relations existed in between them and on 12.05.2024 without informing her family members, she left home with the applicant, who took her to Pilibhit and dropped her to railway Ashish Harijan vs The State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home ...

1 station, from where she called her father and went back home.
After the victim went back home, the victim committed suicide on 28.05.2024.
The cause of death as per the post mortem report in ante mortem hanging and apart from a ligature mark, scratch wounds were found on the fore-arm and abdomen.
3. The counsel for the applicant argues that the applicant is being prosecuted for the offences under Sections 305/376 IPC without there being no material to implicate him.
He further argues that the suicide was committed by the victim when she was at her parents home and there is no material to suggest abetment at the instance of the applicant.
4. Learned A.G.A. opposed the bail prayer by arguing that as the applicant had left the victim despite taking her together at the railway station, she committed suicide.
There is no suicide note on record.

5. Considering the arguments, prima facie, the material to implicate the applicant under the offences particularly for the offence under Section 305 IPC is missing as there is no material to suggest abetment at the instance of the applicant, even for the offence under Section 376 IPC, there is no material as the victim herself had admitted physical relation existed in between them.
Considering all these facts coupled with the fact that the applicant is in custody since 15.05.2024 and has no criminal history in enlarged on bail.
Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.

6. Let the applicant Ashish Harijan be released on bail in FIR/ Case Crime No. 0160 of 2024, under Sections 363, 366-A, 376, 305 IPC and Section 5/6 POCSO Act, Police Station Lambhua, District Sultanpur, on his furnishing personal bonds and two reliable sureties of Rs.20,000/- each to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:
(a) The applicant shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
(b) The applicant shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which he is accused or suspected of the commission; and (c) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
Order Date :- 13.8.2024 Arun  Ashish Harijan vs The State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home ... on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/188220062/
